subject: community-medicine
title: Lymphatic Filariasis: Vector, Microfilaraemia and Mass Chemotherapy

steps.title: Parasite biology and Indian distribution
steps.tx: Across endemic districts of India, **lymphatic filariasis** represents a major cause of preventable permanent physical disability and social stigma. The nematode Wuchereria bancrofti accounts for over ninety-nine percent of all cases nationwide, causing extensive genital and lower limb involvement, whereas Brugia malayi produces less than one percent of cases, restricted to isolated rural pockets in coastal Kerala, Odisha and Assam, sparing the genitalia.
steps.say: Wuchereria bancrofti causes ninety-nine percent of Indian filariasis, affecting the legs and genitals. Brugia malayi causes the remaining one percent in isolated rural pockets, sparing the genitalia.

right.title: Brugia malayi (<1%)
points: Restricted to pockets in Kerala and Odisha

steps.title: Vector bionomics: Culex quinquefasciatus
steps.tx: The domestic culicine mosquito **Culex quinquefasciatus** serves as the principal urban and rural vector of bancroftian filariasis across India. It breeds abundantly in grossly polluted, stagnant, organic-rich wastewater collections, including open roadside masonry drains, septic tanks, sewage overflows, soak pits and cesspools; the female vector feeds aggressively indoors during night hours, resting on hanging clothes and dark corners.
steps.say: Culex quinquefasciatus breeds prolifically in polluted drains, cesspools and open sewage. It bites indoors during late night hours, transmitting microfilariae across families.

rows: Strictly nocturnal, peaking midnight to 2 AM
Dark indoor walls, curtains and clothing

steps.title: Nocturnal periodicity and blood sampling
steps.tx: Diagnostic blood surveys exploit the phenomenon of **nocturnal periodicity**, wherein microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti retreat into deep pulmonary capillaries during daylight hours and surge into peripheral circulation between ten o'clock at night and two o'clock in the morning. Consequently, epidemiological surveillance teams conduct field blood collection exclusively during night surveys, preparing twenty-microlitre thick blood smears stained with Giemsa to detect motile sheathed microfilariae.
steps.say: Microfilariae hide in deep lung vessels by day and enter the bloodstream between ten at night and two in the morning. Blood surveys must be conducted at night to find them.

nodes.label: Giemsa stain and microscopic microfilaria count

steps.tx: The finger prick is taken around midnight because that is when these parasites circulate in the skin blood. **Nocturnal periodicity** means microfilariae of Wuchereria bancrofti retreat into deep pulmonary capillaries by day and surge into peripheral blood between ten at night and two in the morning. Surveillance teams therefore collect blood only on night rounds. They prepare 20 microlitre thick smears and stain them with Giemsa to find motile sheathed microfilariae.
steps.say: Bancroftian microfilariae stay in deep lung vessels during the day and enter the bloodstream from about ten at night until two in the morning. Night teams make thick Giemsa films of 20 microlitres so those sheathed larvae can be seen.

steps.title: Epidemiological indices: microfilaria and endemicity
steps.tx: Programme officers evaluate district transmission using the **microfilaria rate**, which measures the percentage of night blood smears containing microfilariae, with an operational benchmark of less than one percent indicating successful transmission interruption. The Endemicity Rate combines the microfilaria rate with the clinical disease rate, while transmission assessment surveys evaluate antigenemia among six to seven-year-old schoolchildren using immunochromatographic cards.
steps.say: The microfilaria rate is the percentage of people with microfilariae in night blood. Bringing this rate below one percent across communities indicates that transmission has been stopped.

steps.title: Clinical progression: acute adenolymphangitis to elephantiasis
steps.tx: Adult filarial worms reside within afferent lymphatic channels, causing chronic endothelial proliferation, valvular incompetence and lymphatic ectasia that culminate in **elephantiasis**. Repeated episodes of acute adenolymphangitis triggered by secondary bacterial streptococcal invasion accelerate irreversible subcutaneous fibrosis and brawny non-pitting oedema, transforming reversible lymphoedema into massive, verrucous, hyperkeratotic skin enlargement of the lower limbs and scrotum.
steps.say: Adult worms block lymphatic vessels. Secondary bacterial infections trigger repeated attacks of severe pain and swelling, slowly turning soft swelling into hard, permanent elephantiasis.

steps.tx: The limb is massively enlarged and the skin is mossy, the chronic picture called elephantiasis. Adult worms living in afferent lymphatic channels cause endothelial overgrowth, failing valves, and dilated lymphatics that culminate in **elephantiasis**. Repeated acute adenolymphangitis from secondary streptococcal infection drives irreversible subcutaneous fibrosis and brawny nonpitting oedema. Reversible swelling becomes verrucous, hyperkeratotic enlargement of the legs and of the scrotum.
steps.say: Adult filarial worms damage lymphatic valves and widen the channels. Streptococcal attacks of adenolymphangitis then scar the tissue. Soft swelling turns into hard, mossy, permanent enlargement of the leg or scrotum.

vis.alt: An advanced case of elephantiasis shows massive enlargement of a lower limb with mossy, thickened skin.
vis.caption: The lower limb is grossly enlarged and the skin is mossy and verrucous, the chronic lymphatic end stage of filariasis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Mass drug administration strategy
steps.tx: To eliminate the human infectious reservoir, national authorities implement **mass drug administration**, delivering a single annual prophylactic dose of anthelmintics to every resident living in endemic districts, excluding pregnant women, children under two years of age and the severely ill. Sustained population treatment coverage exceeding sixty-five to eighty percent for five to six consecutive years drains circulating microfilariae below vector transmission thresholds.
steps.say: Mass drug administration gives annual preventive tablets to everyone in endemic districts. Treating over eighty percent of the community for five years extinguishes the parasite reservoir.

rows: Single dose administered once every 12 months

Ensures vector mosquitoes encounter no microfilariae

steps.title: Diethylcarbamazine citrate pharmacology and dosing
steps.tx: The synthetic piperazine compound **diethylcarbamazine citrate** forms the bedrock of filariasis chemotherapy, dosed at six milligrams per kilogram body weight in mass campaigns. It alters microfilarial surface membranes to expose hidden antigens to host immune destruction, clearing circulating parasites within forty-eight hours; systemic reactions such as fever, headache and dizziness arise from massive antigen release from dying microfilariae.
steps.say: Diethylcarbamazine exposes parasite membranes so the immune system can destroy them within two days. Mild fever and headache result from the rapid destruction of dying parasites.

left.title: Microfilaricidal effect
points: Prevents vector mosquitoes from getting infected
Triggers transient host fever and headache

right.title: Macrofilaricidal effect
points: Sterilises or slowly kills adult worms
Suppresses new microfilaria output for months

steps.title: Albendazole and ivermectin synergy
steps.tx: Co-administering albendazole at a fixed four-hundred-milligram dose with diethylcarbamazine produces powerful anthelmintic synergy, destroying intestinal geohelminths while crippling adult filarial worms. In non-co-endemic districts, adding **ivermectin co-administration** at two hundred micrograms per kilogram paralyses microfilarial pharyngeal musculature, achieving near-complete clearance of circulating microfilariae that lasts for up to two years.
steps.say: Adding albendazole and ivermectin creates a potent combination. It clears microfilariae for up to two years while simultaneously deworming children of intestinal roundworms.

rows: Unmasks microfilarial antigens to host antibodies
Inhibits worm tubulin polymerisation and deworms
Opens glutamate-gated chloride channels in worms

steps.title: Morbidity management and disability prevention
steps.tx: The second essential pillar of the national program is **morbidity management**, providing comprehensive self-care education and clinical services to patients already suffering from chronic elephantiasis or hydrocele. Patients learn meticulous daily limb hygiene using soap and clean water, prompt topical application of antifungal cream to interdigital fungal cracks, and regular limb elevation, while hospitals offer free surgical eversion and excision for hydroceles.
steps.say: Morbidity management teaches patients to wash swollen limbs with soap and water, treat skin cracks with antifungal cream, and keep limbs elevated. Hospitals provide free hydrocele surgery.

nodes.label: Daily soap and water limb washing
Free surgical repair for scrotal hydrocele
